title: Install the agent skill into the project
lead: The skill command prints markdown to stdout. The agent reference tells a person to copy it by hand into the Claude, Codex, and Grok skill paths.
findings_note: another project: slicer ai skill prints a SKILL.md and does not write it anywhere
boundary: **Not in this slice:** installing into the home directory or into `.codex/skills/`; symlinking to the slicer repo's skill file; changing the skill wording.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: A handoff project needs the adapted skill from the finish setting, not a copy of this repo's generic `skills/slicer/SKILL.md`. The command has to write the text it would have printed. Codex already reads `.agents/skills/`, so a fourth `.codex` copy is unnecessary.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. Without a write flag, stdout is still the skill text, including a loaded project's finish mode.
2. `--output PATH` writes exactly that text and creates missing parent directories.
3. `--install` writes that text to `.claude/skills/slicer/SKILL.md`, `.agents/skills/slicer/SKILL.md`, and `.grok/skills/slicer/SKILL.md` under the project root.
4. An existing destination that already equals the text is rewritten cleanly. Different contents exit 2 with code `state` and write nothing, unless `--force`.
5. The command does not symlink and does not read `skills/slicer/SKILL.md` from disk. `--json` reports the paths written.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Add `--output` and `--install` on the skill command, plus `--force` for a destination that already holds different text. Write the bytes the command prints. Create parent directories. On a refusal, leave every destination unchanged.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The failing tests pass, then `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests`, `slicer check`, and `git diff --check`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch, including the re-rendered roadmap and a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased.
